data.narrative:
Interlune is a seed-stage space & aerospace company founded by Rob Meyerson, Gary Lai, and Harrison Schmitt, having raised $23M to date. The target operates within a sector containing 5 public comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, ICEYE, Sierra Space, and Planet Labs.

Standard valuation triangulation methods yield limited utility here. Peer-median analysis is inapplicable: while 14 same-sector peers exist in the Space & Aerospace universe, zero satisfy the filters for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier comparability. Public-comp anchoring cannot proceed, as Interlune's revenue is not disclosed—a typical constraint for private companies—and applying the sector P/S median of 25.3x across 6 public tickers would be unfounded without this input.

The absence of narrow-set peer data and material financial disclosures prevents triangulated valuation synthesis at this stage. A defensible valuation range requires either: (1) Interlune's revenue or near-term revenue guidance; (2) identification of private peers with disclosed financials and similar funding stage; or (3) qualitative framework anchored to capital deployed ($23M) and anticipated use of proceeds. Analysts should flag that seed-stage space ventures exhibit wide valuation dispersion, and further diligence into Interlune's technical and commercial milestones would be prerequisite to any pricing recommendation.
